posts.text:
Your ferritin is "normal". Your thyroid is "normal". You're still exhausted.

Normal means above the disease threshold, not optimal. Ferritin clears the lab range at 13 ug/L. Sustained energy needs 70+.

And the NHS doesn't test fasting insulin at all.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/fatigue-energy

Most labs flag testosterone as normal from 8.7 nmol/L. Optimal is above 15.

That gap is where men live with fatigue, low libido, poor sleep and brain fog for years, being told they're fine.

In women it's barely tested at all.

https://veridianclinic.com/assessments

Perimenopause doesn't start at 50. For many women it starts mid-30s, years before periods change.

By the time FSH rises enough for an NHS diagnosis, most have spent years being told they're fine.

FSH, LH ratio, oestradiol and AMH map exactly where you are.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/womens-hormones

Eating less. Exercising more. Weight not moving.

That's not willpower. Four testable reasons:

- high fasting insulin (fat-storage mode)
- cortisol dysregulation (visceral fat)
- sub-optimal thyroid (slowed metabolism)
- insulin resistance

None appear on a standard NHS review.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/metabolic-weight

1 in 5 people carry elevated Lp(a). It doubles cardiovascular risk independently of LDL.

Almost none of them know, because it's never on a standard cholesterol panel. Statins, diet and exercise don't lower it.

Family history of early heart disease? Test this first.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/cardiovascular-risk

Insulin resistance develops silently for a decade before fasting glucose rises.

You can be on the road to type 2 while every NHS test says normal.

The early marker: fasting insulin. Optimal is under 8 mIU/L. Labs don't flag it until 24.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/fasting-insulin

Homocysteine above 10 umol/L damages artery walls, accelerates cognitive decline and drives nerve injury.

It's on zero standard NHS panels. And the fix is usually just targeted B12, folate and B6, within weeks.

Included in our Cardiovascular Risk Panel (£349):
https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/cardiovascular-risk

The NHS calls vitamin D "sufficient" above 50 nmol/L.

That's the level that prevents rickets. It's a disease threshold, not a health target. Research on immunity, bone density, mood and testosterone points to 100-150.

Most UK adults spend winter below 50.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/fatigue-energy

Cutting calories. Training 3x a week. Weight still creeping up around your middle.

Not a discipline problem. The usual driver is insulin resistance, where fasting glucose and HbA1c still read as normal.

Standard NHS panels rarely measure fasting insulin.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/fatigue-energy

"Your HbA1c is fine" might be the most misleading sentence in metabolic medicine.

HbA1c only rises once glucose is already high. Insulin resistance can run for a DECADE before that, while your body drowns the problem in extra insulin.

The earlier marker: fasting insulin.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/fasting-insulin

A number you've never had tested predicts cardiovascular death better than your cholesterol panel.

Omega-3 index above 8% = roughly 90% lower risk of sudden cardiac death vs below 4%. Linked to ~5 extra years of life. The UK average sits near the bottom.

And it's fixable in months: ~2g EPA/DHA daily.

https://veridianclinic.com/blog/omega-3

Chronological age: how long you've been alive.
Biological age: how fast you're actually ageing.

The gap between them is measurable, and closable. A 52-year-old with the biology of 62 has a specific problem to solve, and a decade to solve it.

150+ markers: https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/biological-age

Brain fog at 45 is not "just getting older". Four markers explain most cases:

- Free T3 below 5 pmol/L
- Ferritin below 70 ug/L
- B12 below 500 pmol/L
- Fasting insulin above 8 mIU/L

All treatable. None on a standard NHS panel.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/fatigue-energy

Mounjaro and Wegovy work. They work better aimed at the right problem.

Before starting any GLP-1 I'd want: fasting insulin, full thyroid panel, morning cortisol, HbA1c + HOMA-IR.

Is it insulin resistance, thyroid, or stress-driven fat? Different answers, different plans.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/metabolic-weight

For the professional in their 40s-50s: gained weight despite eating well, exhausted by 2pm, told your bloods are "normal".

You're not lazy. You're not imagining it.

Fasting insulin, morning cortisol, Free T3, testosterone. Four markers that tell a different story.

Free 3-min check: https://veridianclinic.com/metabolic-quiz

Belly fat in your 40s is not the weight you carried at 25.

It's visceral fat: metabolically active, inflammatory, and a cardiovascular risk independent of BMI.

Drivers: rising fasting insulin, cortisol dysregulation, declining testosterone. All three testable.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/metabolic-weight

Question for UK professionals: has your GP ever run a fasting insulin test on you?

A) Yes, recently
B) Years ago
C) Never offered
D) What's that?

It catches insulin resistance a decade before glucose rises. If you answered C or D, you're the majority, and that's the problem.

https://veridianclinic.com/blood-tests/fasting-insulin

The conversation I have most as a GP:

"All my bloods came back fine. But I feel terrible."

NHS tests rule out disease. Normal = above the disease threshold, not optimal.

Ferritin 13 passes; energy needs 70+. Fasting insulin isn't tested at all.

That gap is measurable. https://veridianclinic.com

Told you're pre-diabetic? The standard pathway is: lose weight, cut carbs, come back in a year.

What it misses:
- the insulin resistance actually driving it
- thyroid suppression that blocks weight loss
- overnight liver glucose output

All three treatable. https://veridianclinic.com

Your father: heart attack at 54. Your mother: type 2 at 52.

You can't change your genetics. You can know exactly which risks you inherited: ApoB, Lp(a), fasting insulin, HbA1c + HOMA-IR.

And start acting 20 years earlier than your parents could.
